title: Fourteen Evenings and One Unfinished Sentence
subtitle: 观点与交流 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 观点与交流（做人与做事·观点表达与交流）
meta: 主题语境：观点与交流（做人与做事·观点表达与交流）　|　核心词汇：discussion　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 discussion 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the chairman ① opened a discussion that no member in the hall would have joined, and he said the opening was the whole of the evening. The ② discussion, meaning the talking and not the debate, ran fourteen evenings and stayed unminuted in the book; a discussion, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left unwritten.

Every ③ discussion in that hall had the same unfinished sentence at the end of it, and the ④ discussion at the end, meaning the one they kept for the new members and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever attended twice. A discussion, the secretary said, is nine parts listening and one part somebody willing to open; the chairman said the listening is the part that fills fourteen evenings.

The reporter meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the discussion was the whole of the article, meaning the debate and not the talking. The ⑥ discussion, meaning the debate and not any of that, is the only thing in an article that everybody summarises and nobody settles; discussion, he said, is either something you open or the only word that means both a talking and a debate. He said the debate is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ discussion had become a line in a newsletter, and the newsletter had become an argument about the unfinished sentence. The ⑧ discussion of the whole thing, the chairman wrote in October, was one hall and fourteen evenings of listening; discussion, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to listen. She said the listening was never mentioned.

The ⑨ discussion I remember is the one at the end, which was resumed in 1970 and is still described as the longest in the hall. A ⑩ discussion, the secretary said in 1972, is the only thing that improves by being listened to; every discussion, she said, is a debate that has agreed to look like a talking. She said the debate was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 讨论；商议（指礼堂里进行的那一场）
B. n. 讨论（指那些交谈本身，与那场辩论相对）
C. 固定搭配：open a discussion 开启一场讨论
D. n. 讨论（指留给新成员用的那一场）
E. n. 讨论；议论（抽象总称，指一座礼堂的讨论之事）
F. n. 讨论（指简讯里写到、被记下的那一场）
G. n. 辩论；争论（指文章里被概述的那场）
H. n. 争论（抽象总称，指人人概述却无人平息的那场）

items.q: opened a discussion that no member in the hall would have joined
The discussion, meaning the talking and not the debate
the discussion was the whole of the article
the discussion had become a line in a newsletter
The discussion of the whole thing
A discussion, the secretary said in 1972

answers.why: open a discussion 意为“开启一场讨论”，1949 年主席开启了一场礼堂里没有一位成员肯参加讨论。
discussion 意为“讨论”，指那些交谈本身而不是那场辩论，它进行了十四个晚上而记录簿上没有记载。
discussion 意为“讨论、商议”，指那座礼堂里每一场讨论，每一场末尾都有同一句没说完的话。
discussion 意为“讨论”，指留给新成员用的那一场，是唯一有人参加过两次的。
discussion 意为“辩论、争论”，指文章里被概述的那场，记者说这场争论就是那篇文章的全部。
discussion 意为“争论”，指人人概述却无人平息的那场而不是那些交谈本身，是文章里人人都概述、却无人平息的东西。
discussion 意为“讨论”，指简讯里写到、被记下的那一场，到 1957 年这场讨论成了简讯里的一行。
discussion 意为“讨论、议论”，主席十月写道，整件事的讨论之事是一座礼堂和十四个晚上的倾听。
discussion 意为“讨论”，我记得的是末尾那一场，1970 年重启，至今仍被说成礼堂里最长的一场。
discussion 为抽象总称，秘书 1972 年说，一场讨论是唯一会因为被认真倾听而变得更好的东西。
